projects.name: Frontier AI Valuation Lab
projects.summary: A valuation and financing model for frontier AI labs that compares funding plans against a capital goal and an ownership floor, with a seeded Monte Carlo range for value.
projects.scenario: Open the worked decision and raise the ownership floor from 88% to 90%: only Plan A still qualifies. Then open the Monte Carlo panel and look at the median and the spread of value around the Anthropic Base case.
projects.inspect: The financial math is plain JavaScript shared by the browser and a Node.js API, which return byte-identical JSON for the same Monte Carlo request. Separate Python scripts recompute the capital and uncertainty arithmetic.
projects.limits: Illustrative assumptions and incomplete public data, with no affiliation to the companies named. Simulated percentiles describe the ranges entered, not a forecast.
projects.command:
npm test
python3 -B scripts/check_uncertainty_reference.py --output /tmp/uncertainty-reference.json
npm start

projects.name: crossbook
projects.summary: An order-matching engine in Rust with call auctions, crash recovery, a market-data feed and multi-instrument sharding, checked against a second, simpler engine.
projects.scenario: Run the auction demo. An opening call collects orders without trading, prints the indicative uncross after each one and rejects an immediate-or-cancel order. The uncross then fills 13 lots at 101, market orders first.
projects.inspect: Start with the one-pass clearing-price search, then the brute-force uncross that tries every price. The two agree on 20,000 random books, including ties at each rule.
projects.limits: Books live in memory in one process, journals are written without fsync, and there is no network gateway or market connection. The clearing price is always one of the orders’ limits, and there are no volatility interruptions.
projects.command:
cargo run --release -p crossbook-cli -- demo
cargo run --release -p crossbook-cli -- auction
cargo run --release -p crossbook-cli -- verify --orders 1000000

projects.name: LineageGuard Studio
projects.summary: Reviews a database schema change against the lineage it affects, with evidence from fixtures, DataHub or a dbt manifest, and resumes a run that crashed.
projects.scenario: Review a column rename against a dbt manifest from a synthetic project. Renaming fct_mrr.mrr_usd lists five downstream models and two exposures with their owners. The decision stays at needs-evidence, because a manifest cannot show usage.
projects.inspect: Start with the manifest adapter, which refuses unknown versions, cycles and graphs whose edge lists disagree. A seeded property test compares its lineage with an independent walk of depends_on.
projects.limits: Synthetic data, and the optional DataHub capture is read-only. Lineage from a manifest is model-level, so it can block a change or ask for more evidence but never clear one. A passing export check means internal consistency, not approval.
projects.command:
npm run studio:review -- --dbt-manifest=public/studio/dbt/saas-analytics-warehouse/manifest.json --dbt-catalog=public/studio/dbt/saas-analytics-warehouse/catalog.json --request=examples/dbt/rename-mrr-usd.json --output=./.lineageguard/dbt-review.json
npm run studio:benchmark -- --check
# Use new export paths when repeating; existing outputs are never overwritten.

projects.name: SaaS Analytics Warehouse
projects.summary: A dbt and DuckDB warehouse for a fictional SaaS company: MRR, retention and unit economics, with incremental loads and type 2 subscription history.
projects.scenario: Build the warehouse, then load the same rows day by day with late arrivals and check that the incremental build equals a full refresh. Or trace one month of churn from the MRR bridge to the customers behind it.
projects.inspect: Start with the 7-day lookback macro and the delete+insert staging models, then the snapshot and its four history tests. The load simulation compares 24 relations with a full refresh by row hash.
projects.limits: Seeded fictional data. Rows more than 7 days late are missed until a full refresh, the marts still rebuild in full, and incremental runs are not faster at this size.
projects.command:
uv sync --locked
make data build MONTHS=24 SCALE=0.25
uv run python -m saasreport.churn --month 2024-12 --output-dir ../tallyloom-churn-2024-12
make incremental-check MONTHS=6 SCALE=0.25 DAILY_DAYS=14

projects.name: Impact Ledger
projects.summary: Attendance and spending reports for a fictional nonprofit, with a local API, atomic CSV imports and a hash-chained audit log that rebuilds past reports.
projects.scenario: Import sessions and attendance, rebuild the summary as it was before the attendance import, undo that import with a compensating batch, then verify the log. The undone import stays in the history.
projects.inspect: Start with the audit log, written in the same SQLite transaction as each change. Triggers block edits and deletions, and verify detects edited, deleted or reordered entries.
projects.limits: The hosted preview is read-only and synthetic. The log is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof, and actor labels are self-declared.
projects.command:
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db init
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db import sessions examples/sessions.csv
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db import attendance examples/attendance.csv
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db summary --as-of-entry 2
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db undo-import B000003
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db verify

projects.name: ContrastKit
projects.summary: Color contrast checks, hue-preserving fixes and color-vision simulation at any severity, as a library, a CLI and a web app.
projects.scenario: Check a green and red pair under deuteranomaly at severity 0.6 and under deuteranopia, then move the severity slider in the Palette Auditor.
projects.inspect: Start with the interpolation between the published 0.1-step matrices of Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes. The results agree with colorspacious and DaltonLens.
projects.limits: Contrast checks support accessibility work but are not a full audit. Severity is a model parameter, not a clinical measure, and tritan simulations are the least reliable.
projects.command:
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
npx contrastkit check 2f855a c53030 --cvd deuteranomaly:0.6 --cvd deuteranopia

projects.name: MOTIONX Studio
projects.summary: The website for my motion-design studio, plus a Python tool that drafts outreach emails and leaves sending to a person.
projects.scenario: Browse the site at phone and desktop widths, with reduced motion on and off, then read how the outreach validator decides PASS or FAIL.
projects.inspect: Start with the Playwright tests for the site and the outreach tests, which run on fictional companies.
projects.limits: The films on the site are concept work, not client commissions. The outreach tool drafts email and never sends it.
projects.command:
npm ci
npm run dev -- -p 3939

projects.name: RelayBox
projects.summary: A durable webhook inbox that deduplicates deliveries and fences stale workers, plus outbound delivery signed per the Standard Webhooks specification.
projects.scenario: Deliver a message to the example receiver. The first attempt gets 503 with Retry-After, and the retry succeeds with the same webhook-id. The inbound demo sends one signed event twice and shows retries, leases and recovery.
projects.inspect: Start with the dispatcher: full-jitter backoff, the dead-letter queue and replay. Signing matches the specification’s published test vector, and a sender killed mid-request leaves its lease for another to resend.
projects.limits: A single-host SQLite service. Outbound targets are loopback-only unless you allow others, there is no rate limit or circuit breaker, and signing secrets are stored unencrypted.
projects.command:
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/demo.sqlite3 demo
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/demo.sqlite3 serve --demo-secret
# Outbound: start the receiver in one terminal, then deliver from another
python3 examples/receive_webhooks.py --demo-secret --fail-first 1
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/out.sqlite3 subscription add http://127.0.0.1:8788/hook --event-type example.created --demo-secret
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/out.sqlite3 publish example.created examples/payload.json
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/out.sqlite3 deliver --max-deliveries 10 --wait 15

projects.name: TraceBench
projects.summary: Offline evaluation of recorded AI outputs, with cost accounting and statistical regression gates.
projects.scenario: Compare two candidates against a 100-case synthetic baseline. The default gate fails both, while the McNemar gate passes the noisy candidate and fails the regressed one.
projects.inspect: Start with the exact McNemar test and the paired bootstrap behind the --gate options. In a simulation where 10% of cases flip at random, the default gate failed 99.4% of unchanged suites.
projects.limits: It scores recorded outputs and never calls a model. Gates judge pass or fail only and assume independent cases.
projects.command:
mkdir -p reports
python3 -m tracebench evaluate --cases fixtures/paired/cases.jsonl --outputs fixtures/paired/baseline.jsonl --pricing fixtures/pricing.json --report reports/paired-baseline.json
python3 -m tracebench evaluate --cases fixtures/paired/cases.jsonl --outputs fixtures/paired/noisy.jsonl --pricing fixtures/pricing.json --baseline reports/paired-baseline.json --gate mcnemar
python3 -m tracebench evaluate --cases fixtures/paired/cases.jsonl --outputs fixtures/paired/regressed.jsonl --pricing fixtures/pricing.json --baseline reports/paired-baseline.json --gate mcnemar --format markdown

projects.name: quantkit
projects.summary: Option pricing, portfolio optimization, backtesting and VaR model validation, checked against textbook values and exact calculations.
projects.scenario: Simulate fictional prices, forecast one-day 99% VaR each day, and backtest the forecasts with Kupiec’s and Christoffersen’s tests, the Basel traffic light and the Acerbi–Székely Z2 test.
projects.inspect: Start with the four rolling forecasters, then the dynamic program that gives each backtest its exact size. A perturbation test keeps every forecast blind to the return it is scored against.
projects.limits: Educational software on synthetic data, not investment advice. VaR covers one day and one return series, and the likelihood-ratio p-values are asymptotic.
projects.command:
uv sync
uv run quantkit simulate --output prices.csv
uv run quantkit var-backtest prices.csv --method ewma --level 0.99

projects.name: powerlift
projects.summary: Experiment statistics: power analysis, A/B/n tests with Dunnett’s correction, CUPED, sequential monitoring and Bayesian tools.
projects.scenario: Read a seeded CSV with one control and three variants. The sample-ratio check runs across all four arms, and Dunnett’s test finds only variant D different while keeping the family-wise false-win rate at 5%.
projects.inspect: Start with the many-to-one analysis, where the shared control turns a k-dimensional integral into a two-dimensional one. Results agree with scipy.stats.dunnett.
projects.limits: Results depend on study design and data assumptions, and a significant result alone is not a business decision. Multi-arm comparisons are many-to-one and pool the arms’ variance.
projects.command:
uv sync
uv run python examples/multi_arm_simulation.py --csv arms.csv
uv run powerlift analyze --csv arms.csv --group-col arm --value-col revenue_usd --control-label A --treatment-label B --treatment-label C --treatment-label D

projects.name: ledgerline
projects.summary: A double-entry ledger API with balanced, immutable entries, idempotent writes and holds that report ledger, held and available balances.
projects.scenario: Follow the API walkthrough. Place a hold and watch the available balance fall while the ledger balance stays put, capture part of it, void another and let one expire.
projects.inspect: Start with the account version check that holds and postings share. In the race test, 33 of 40 concurrent holds succeed, the most the balance allows.
projects.limits: An engineering demo, not a bank, payment processor or certified accounting system. A hold allows one capture, and expiry is computed when a hold is read.
projects.command:
uv sync
uv run python examples/wallet_demo.py
uv run pytest tests/test_holds_concurrency.py -v

projects.name: searchlite
projects.summary: A full-text search engine in TypeScript with compressed postings, top-k pruning that never changes a ranking, explainable scores and relevance evaluation.
projects.scenario: Compare two saved indexes against your own relevance judgments in the browser and look for queries that got worse. Then run the pruning property tests, which compare pruned results with scoring every match.
projects.inspect: Start with the blocks of 128 documents, their score bounds and the MaxScore windows built on them. On 10,000 synthetic documents, pruning made median queries 7 to 15 times faster.
projects.limits: A small in-memory library with English-only analysis. Block-max WAND is not implemented, and one phrase-heavy query is slower with pruning.
projects.command:
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build
npx vitest run test/engine/pruning.test.ts
searchlite_review_dir=$(mktemp -d)
searchlite_review_dir=$(cd "$searchlite_review_dir" && pwd -P)
node examples/search-docs.js index examples/fixtures/relevance-notes "$searchlite_review_dir/notes.json"
node examples/search-docs.js evaluate "$searchlite_review_dir/notes.json" examples/fixtures/relevance-notes/judgments.json

projects.name: citecheck
projects.summary: Question answering over your documents with cited sources and a checker that flags claims the sources do not support.
projects.scenario: Index the sample handbook and ask a question whose prepared answer flips a negation. The word-overlap checker calls the sentence supported; the claim-level checker flags it.
projects.inspect: Start with claim splitting, clause alignment and the negation, modality, opposite-word and quantity checks. On held-out cases the claim-level checker caught 44 of 48 unsupported sentences. Word overlap caught 20.
projects.limits: The offline responses are hand-written, and one author wrote both the cases and the rules, so the figures are optimistic. Live answers need your own API key.
projects.command:
uv sync
uv run citecheck index examples/handbook
uv run citecheck ask "Do I need a doctor's note when I take a sick day?"
uv run citecheck eval-claims

projects.name: ProofCast
projects.summary: Local media generation with provenance records, Ed25519 manifest signatures and a Merkle transparency log.
projects.scenario: Generate a local bundle, then run the tamper demo. It signs and logs the bundle on copies and catches a changed media byte, a changed manifest, a different key, a flipped proof bit and a rewritten log entry.
projects.inspect: Start with the RFC 6962 and RFC 9162 Merkle tree and its inclusion and consistency proofs. They match 195 of 196 published transparency-dev/merkle vectors; the last one uses placeholder roots and is rejected on purpose.
projects.limits: A signature proves which key signed, not who holds it. The log is one local file without witnesses, the private key is stored unencrypted, and the optional B2 upload has not run against a real bucket.
projects.command:
.venv/bin/python -m proofcast.cli --title "Synthetic demo" --script "A local verification example."
.venv/bin/python examples/tamper_demo.py output/YOUR-RUN-ID-manifest.json

projects.name: Luma Keys
projects.summary: An offline piano practice app with sheet music, falling notes, planned fingering on 3-D hands and graded sight reading.
projects.scenario: Generate a sight-reading exercise, play a clean run and a flawed one, then check the saved progress and repeat the same seed.
projects.inspect: Run the five sight-reading browser stories and look at their screenshots and the practice grading, which needs none of the optional engines.
projects.limits: The browser tests use synthetic exercises with the 3-D hands turned off. A physical MIDI keyboard, the packaged app and the optional engines need separate checks.
projects.command:
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npx playwright install chromium --only-shell
npm test
npm run qa:browser -- --output-dir .qa-runs/reviewer-exercise

projects.name: Blast Radius Daily
projects.summary: A one-minute Reddit puzzle about stopping a bad schema change from spreading, playable with a mouse or a keyboard.
projects.scenario: Pick an incident day and place two circuit breakers with the mouse, or with Tab, the arrow keys and Space. Watch the cascade, compare your result, move one synthetic vote, then delete your local data and replay.
projects.inspect: Open the offline build, or build it yourself. Start with the shared engine and the hidden accessible copy of the board that keyboard and screen-reader players use.
projects.limits: A desktop and landscape demo whose community data lives in the tab and resets on reload. Keyboard and screen-reader support is checked with Playwright and axe-core in Chromium, not with a real screen reader or inside Reddit’s apps.
projects.command:
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build:demo
# Open dist-demo/blast-radius-demo.html from disk
npx playwright install chromium --only-shell
npm run test:demo

projects.name: Agentic Trading Research
projects.summary: A snapshot of a research-only trading system, with a runnable review gate and backtest-overfitting diagnostics. It cannot place orders.
projects.scenario: Run the overfitting demo. The best of 100 no-skill strategies has a naive PSR of 0.9989, yet all four diagnostics flag it, and a strategy with injected skill passes them all. Then run the six gate scenarios.
projects.inspect: Start with the standard-library PSR, DSR, CSCV, stationary bootstrap and SPA code. The tests reproduce the DSR paper’s worked example and compare PBO with a brute-force version.
projects.limits: Synthetic data only, with no orders, brokerage connection or trading advice. Passing these diagnostics does not show that a strategy is profitable.
projects.command:
python3 -B examples/overfitting_demo.py
python3 -B examples/fail_closed_gate.py --all
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s examples -p "test_*.py" -v

projects.name: JUST-QR
projects.summary: A small browser QR generator with its own ISO/IEC 18004 encoder and image export.
projects.scenario: Make a QR code at the default level H, try a link that is too long, then lower the level until it fits and compare the clipboard and download images.
projects.inspect: Start with qr.js: Reed-Solomon coding with block interleaving, format and version information, and mask choice by the four penalty rules. Tests match the ISO and zxing vectors and decode random symbols with jsQR.
projects.limits: A QR code encodes what you type and does not check whether the link is safe. One segment per code, with no ECI, Kanji, Micro QR or structured append. The page requests two Google Fonts and must be served over HTTP.
projects.command:
python3 -m http.server 8000
npm ci
npx playwright install chromium --only-shell
npm test

projects.name: Teen Budgeting
projects.summary: A classroom budgeting app built on fictional examples.
projects.scenario: Walk through the budgeting flow and compare the categories and totals on screen with the source.
projects.inspect: Start with the course setup, the server routes and the frontend interactions.
projects.limits: Coursework with fictional data, no persistent sign-in and no real financial accounts.
projects.command:
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
npm run dev
